Title: MongoDB
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-6.5/connectors/connector-specific-documentation/mongodb
Content: Description

Running the MongoDB Connector in Standalone mode will run one execution of the Connector with the specified configuration options and then stop. The output model will be named and published to the host Solidatus site according to the configuration options provided as command line parameters. Any command line arguments not passed will be set to default arguments (Null or empty).

Example

Command line execution example for MongoDB:

java -jar target/solidatus-mongodb-0.0.2-SNAPSHOT.jar \
--spring.profiles.active="standalone" \
--spring.data.mongodb.uri=mongodb://username:password@hostname:port/dbname[?authSource=admin] \
--solidatus.mongodb.databases=local,admin,mydb \
--solidatus.api.host={$SOLIDATUS_HOST}\
--solidatus.api.token={$SOLIDATUS_TOKEN} \
--solidatus.api.model-name="MongoDB Model"
Title: Model Output
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-6.5/connectors/connector-specific-documentation/mongodb/model-output
Content: The MongoDB connector uses MongoDB's API to extract database and collection metadata for the construction of a Solidatus model representative of customers' MongoDB instance.

Title: Connector framework
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-2026.1/connectors/connectors-overview/connectors-framework
Content: Installation

MongoDB requirement: MongoDB replicaset enabled (https://docs.mongodb.com/manual/replication/)

MongoDB requirement: change streams (https://docs.mongodb.com/manual/changeStreams/)

Solidatus UI: websockets is recommended for the best user experience

Connectors are distributed as Docker images or Helm charts, and can also be distributed as zip, jar, “exe” if necessary

Using connectors

Connector jobs run outside of the Solidatus main application process

Each connector has its own agent process

Each connector defines and requires its own job configuration and user interface metadata

Each connector (such as the JDBC connector) can have multiple agents running at the same time

Multiple jobs can run for an agent at the same time as determined by the connector (this is supported by the SDK)

The stages of every job run can be followed and the results are available through the user interface
